source_refs.note: Exercise 11.2, Question 1 (book page 211): graphs of 6 functions on given intervals, parts (i)-(vi). Answer key PDF 309 gives small graphs only; ours are plotted from the functions. Solution book PDF 1003-1015.

blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = -\sin 2x,\ x \in [-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
A graph question: \(y = -\sin 2x\) is the sine wave squeezed (the 2) and turned upside down (the minus).
Plan: amplitude and period, a table for one period \([0, \pi]\), then repeat it 4 times over \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
steps:
Given: \(y = -\sin 2x\), \(x \in [-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
To find / draw: its graph on this interval.
Method: find the amplitude and the period, take x-values a quarter period apart (and halfway between), make a table of values, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve, repeating the pattern over the whole interval.

Amplitude, period and number of cycles
\[\text{Amplitude} = |-1| = 1\]
\[\text{Period} = \dfrac{2\pi}{2} = \pi\]
\[\text{Cycles} = \dfrac{4\pi}{\pi} = 4\]
Why: \(y\) stays between \(-1\) and \(1\); the angle \(2x\) completes \(2\pi\) when \(x\) moves \(\pi\); the interval has length \(2\pi - (-2\pi) = 4\pi\).

Choose x-values for one period
Quarter period \(= \pi/4\); we also take the points halfway between, so \(x = 0, \pi/8, \pi/4, \ldots, \pi\).
Why: zeros, maxima and minima occur a quarter period apart; the halfway points shape the curve.

Work out the table values (the table is shown below the answer)
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}:\ y = -\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} = -1\]
\[x = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}:\ y = -\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{2} = 1\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{8}:\ y = -\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} \approx -0.71\]
Why: first double \(x\) to get the angle, then take its sine, then change the sign.

Values for negative \(x\)
\[y(-x) = -\sin(-2x) = \sin 2x = -y(x)\]
\[x = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}:\ y = 1\]
Why: the function is odd, so for negative \(x\) the table values just change sign; the pattern also repeats every \(\pi\).

Plot and join
Mark \(x\) from \(-2\pi\) to \(2\pi\) in steps of \(\pi/4\) and \(y\) from \(-1\) to \(1\). Plot the points and join them with a smooth wave.
The curve crosses the x-axis at every multiple of \(\pi/2\), has minima \(-1\) at \(x = -7\pi/4, -3\pi/4, \pi/4, 5\pi/4\) and maxima \(1\) at \(x = -5\pi/4, -\pi/4, 3\pi/4, 7\pi/4\).
Why: starting from \(x = 0\) the curve first goes down (the minus sign), unlike \(\sin 2x\) which first goes up.

Check
\[x = \dfrac{7\pi}{4}:\ y = -\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{2}\]
\[= -(-1) = 1\]
Why: \(7\pi/2 = 2\pi + 3\pi/2\) and \(\sin(3\pi/2) = -1\), so the last maximum is where the graph shows it.
blocks.final_answer: An upside-down sine wave of amplitude 1 and period \(\pi\): 4 complete cycles on \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\), zeros at multiples of \(\pi/2\), minima \(-1\) at \(x = -7\pi/4, -3\pi/4, \pi/4, 5\pi/4\), maxima \(1\) at \(x = -5\pi/4, -\pi/4, 3\pi/4, 7\pi/4\).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = -sin 2x from -2 pi to 2 pi: an upside-down sine wave of height 1 making four complete cycles, crossing the x-axis at every multiple of pi/2.
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (i): y = −sin 2x on [−2π, 2π] (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = 2\cos 2x,\ x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
A graph question: the 2 in front doubles the height, the 2 inside halves the period.
Plan: amplitude 2, period \(\pi\); table for \([0, \pi]\), then repeat once more up to \(2\pi\).
steps:
Given: \(y = 2\cos 2x\), \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
To find / draw: its graph on this interval.
Method: find the amplitude and the period, take x-values a quarter period apart (and halfway between), make a table of values, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve, repeating the pattern over the whole interval.

Amplitude, period and number of cycles
\[\text{Amplitude} = 2\]
\[\text{Period} = \dfrac{2\pi}{2} = \pi\]
\[\text{Cycles} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\pi} = 2\]
Why: \(\cos 2x\) lies between \(-1\) and \(1\), so \(2\cos 2x\) lies between \(-2\) and \(2\).

Choose x-values
Quarter period \(= \pi/4\); with halfway points \(x = 0, \pi/8, \ldots, \pi\).
Why: maxima, zeros and minima of a cosine wave come a quarter period apart.

Work out the table values
\[x = 0:\ y = 2\cos 0 = 2\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}:\ y = 2\cos\pi = -2\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{8}:\ y = 2\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} \approx 1.41\]
Why: double \(x\) for the angle, take the cosine, then multiply by 2. For \([\pi, 2\pi]\) the same values repeat.

Plot and join
Mark \(x\) from \(0\) to \(2\pi\) in steps of \(\pi/4\) and \(y\) from \(-2\) to \(2\). Join the points with a smooth wave.
Maxima \(2\) at \(x = 0, \pi, 2\pi\); minima \(-2\) at \(x = \pi/2, 3\pi/2\); zeros at \(x = \pi/4, 3\pi/4, 5\pi/4, 7\pi/4\).
Why: a cosine wave starts at its maximum; the graph begins and ends at height 2.

Check
\[x = \dfrac{7\pi}{4}:\ y = 2\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{2} = 0\]
Why: \(7\pi/2 = 2\pi + 3\pi/2\) and \(\cos(3\pi/2) = 0\), so the last zero is at \(7\pi/4\).
blocks.final_answer: A cosine wave of amplitude 2 and period \(\pi\): 2 complete cycles on \([0, 2\pi]\), maxima \(2\) at \(x = 0, \pi, 2\pi\), minima \(-2\) at \(x = \pi/2, 3\pi/2\), zeros at \(x = \pi/4, 3\pi/4, 5\pi/4, 7\pi/4\).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = 2 cos 2x from 0 to 2 pi: a cosine wave of height 2 making two complete cycles, maxima 2 at 0, pi and 2 pi, minima -2 at pi/2 and 3 pi/2.
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (ii): y = 2 cos 2x on [0, 2π] (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = \tan 2x,\ x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
A tangent graph: it has no maximum or minimum but has vertical asymptotes where \(\tan 2x\) is undefined.
Plan: find the period and the asymptotes, make a table for one branch, then repeat the branch.
steps:
Given: \(y = \tan 2x\), \(x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
To find / draw: its graph on this interval.
Method: period of \(\tan cx\) is \(\pi/c\); asymptotes where the angle is an odd multiple of \(\pi/2\); one branch from a table, then repeated every period.

Period
\[\text{Period} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Why: tangent repeats after \(\pi\) and the angle \(2x\) runs twice as fast as \(x\).

Vertical asymptotes
\[2x = \pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\]
\[x = \pm\dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \pm\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\]
Why: \(\tan\theta = \sin\theta/\cos\theta\) is undefined where \(\cos\theta = 0\), i.e. \(\theta = \pm\pi/2, \pm3\pi/2\). We draw dashed vertical lines there.

Zeros
\[2x = 0,\ \pm\pi,\ \pm2\pi\]
\[x = 0,\ \pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \pm\pi\]
Why: \(\tan\theta = 0\) where \(\sin\theta = 0\).

Table for the middle branch
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{8}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{3} \approx 1.73\]
\[x = -\dfrac{\pi}{8}:\ y = -1\]
Why: tangent is odd, so the negative side has the same values with a minus sign. As \(x \to \pi/4\) the value grows without bound; as \(x \to -\pi/4\) it falls without bound.

Repeat and draw
Copy the branch every \(\pi/2\): full branches on \((-3\pi/4, -\pi/4)\), \((-\pi/4, \pi/4)\), \((\pi/4, 3\pi/4)\), and half branches on \([-\pi, -3\pi/4)\) and \((3\pi/4, \pi]\).
Why: the interval \([-\pi, \pi]\) has length \(2\pi\), which is 4 periods; the two end pieces together make the fourth branch. Each branch rises from left to right and never touches the asymptotes.

Check
\[x = \dfrac{7\pi}{8}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{7\pi}{4} = -1\]
Why: \(7\pi/8 = \pi/2 + 3\pi/8\) lies on the right-hand half branch, which comes up from \(-\infty\) at \(3\pi/4\) to \(0\) at \(\pi\); \(-1\) fits.
blocks.final_answer: Tangent branches of period \(\pi/2\), each rising from left to right, with vertical asymptotes \(x = \pm\pi/4, \pm3\pi/4\) and zeros at \(x = 0, \pm\pi/2, \pm\pi\): three full branches and two half branches at the ends of \([-\pi, \pi]\).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = tan 2x from -pi to pi: rising tangent branches separated by dashed vertical asymptotes at x = -3pi/4, -pi/4, pi/4, 3pi/4, crossing the x-axis at -pi, -pi/2, 0, pi/2, pi.
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (iii): y = tan 2x on [−π, π] with asymptotes dashed (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = \tan \frac{x}{2},\ x \in [-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
A tangent graph stretched sideways: halving the angle doubles the period.
Plan: period and asymptotes, a table, then the branches on \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
steps:
Given: \(y = \tan\frac{x}{2}\), \(x \in [-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
To find / draw: its graph on this interval.
Method: period of \(\tan cx\) is \(\pi/c\); asymptotes where the angle is an odd multiple of \(\pi/2\); table, plot, smooth branches.

Period
\[\text{Period} = \pi \div \dfrac{1}{2} = 2\pi\]
Why: the angle \(x/2\) moves at half the speed of \(x\), so one tangent period \(\pi\) of the angle needs \(2\pi\) in \(x\).

Asymptotes and zeros
\[\dfrac{x}{2} = \pm\dfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x = \pm\pi\]
\[\dfrac{x}{2} = 0, \pm\pi \Rightarrow x = 0, \pm2\pi\]
Why: inside \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\) the angle \(x/2\) runs over \([-\pi, \pi]\), which contains only the odd multiples \(\pm\pi/2\).

Table values
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1\]
\[x = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = -1\]
\[x = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}:\ y = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{3} \approx 1.73\]
Why: halve \(x\) first, then take the tangent; \(3\pi/4\) is in Quadrant II where tangent is negative. Negative \(x\) give the same values with the opposite sign (tangent is odd).

Draw the branches
Full branch on \((-\pi, \pi)\) through the origin, rising from \(-\infty\) to \(+\infty\); half branch on \((\pi, 2\pi]\) rising from \(-\infty\) to \(0\); half branch on \([-2\pi, -\pi)\) rising from \(0\) to \(+\infty\).
Why: the interval has length \(4\pi\), which is 2 periods: one full branch plus two halves.

Check
\[x = -\dfrac{3\pi}{2}:\ y = \tan\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right) = 1\]
Why: on the left half branch the curve goes up from \((-2\pi, 0)\) towards the asymptote \(x = -\pi\); the value \(1\) at \(-3\pi/2\) fits.
blocks.final_answer: Tangent branches of period \(2\pi\) with vertical asymptotes \(x = \pm\pi\) and zeros at \(x = -2\pi, 0, 2\pi\): one full rising branch on \((-\pi, \pi)\) and half branches on \([-2\pi, -\pi)\) and \((\pi, 2\pi]\).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = tan(x/2) from -2 pi to 2 pi: a full rising branch between dashed asymptotes x = -pi and x = pi through the origin, and half branches on [-2 pi, -pi) and (pi, 2 pi].
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (iv): y = tan(x/2) on [−2π, 2π] with asymptotes dashed (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 1 (v) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = \sin \frac{\pi}{2}x,\ x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
Here the coefficient of \(x\) contains \(\pi\), so the period is an ordinary number and the x-axis is marked 0, 1, 2, ...
Plan: period 4, table with step 0.5, plot up to \(2\pi \approx 6.28\).
steps:
Given: \(y = \sin\frac{\pi}{2}x\), \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
To find / draw: its graph on this interval.
Method: find the amplitude and the period, take x-values a quarter period apart (and halfway between), make a table of values, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve, repeating the pattern over the whole interval.

Amplitude, period and cycles
\[\text{Amplitude} = 1\]
\[\text{Period} = 2\pi \div \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 4\]
\[\text{Cycles} = \dfrac{2\pi}{4} \approx 1.57\]
Why: \(2\pi \times 2/\pi = 4\), the \(\pi\)'s cancel; \(2\pi \approx 6.28\) holds one and a half cycles and a little more.

Choose x-values
Quarter period \(= 1\); with halfway points \(x = 0, 0.5, 1, \ldots, 6\) and the end \(x = 2\pi\).
Why: zeros and peaks come 1 unit apart; the half steps shape the curve.

Work out the table values
\[x = 2.5:\ \sin\dfrac{5\pi}{4} = -\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} \approx -0.71\]
\[x = 2\pi:\ \sin(\pi^2) \approx \sin 9.87\]
\[\approx -0.43\]
Why: multiply \(x\) by \(\pi/2\) to get the angle. The last angle \(\pi^2\) is not a standard angle, so use a calculator in radian mode.

Plot and join
Mark \(x\) as ordinary numbers \(0\) to \(6\) (and \(2\pi \approx 6.28\)), \(y\) from \(-1\) to \(1\). Join the points with a smooth wave.
Zeros at \(x = 0, 2, 4, 6\); maxima \(1\) at \(x = 1, 5\); minimum \(-1\) at \(x = 3\); the curve ends at \((2\pi, -0.43)\).
Why: the wave starts at the origin and goes up first, like every sine wave.

Check
\[x = 5:\ \sin\dfrac{5\pi}{2} = \sin\left(2\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 1\]
Why: \(5 = 1 + 4\), one period after the first maximum, so it is again a maximum.
blocks.final_answer: A sine wave of amplitude 1 and period 4: zeros at \(x = 0, 2, 4, 6\), maxima \(1\) at \(x = 1, 5\), minimum \(-1\) at \(x = 3\), ending at \((2\pi, -0.43)\); about \(1\tfrac12\) cycles on \([0, 2\pi]\).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = sin(pi x / 2) from 0 to 2 pi: a sine wave of height 1 and period 4, maxima at x = 1 and 5, minimum at x = 3, zeros at 0, 2, 4, 6, ending at (2 pi, -0.43).
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (v): y = sin(πx/2) on [0, 2π]; x marked in ordinary numbers (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 1 (vi) Draw the graph of each of the following function for the intervals mentioned against each: \(y = \cos \frac{\pi}{2}x,\ x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
blocks.explanation:
A cosine graph whose period is an ordinary number; cosine is even, so the graph is symmetric about the y-axis.
Plan: period 4, table for \(x \ge 0\), mirror it for \(x < 0\).
steps:
Given: \(y = \cos\frac{\pi}{2}x\), \(x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
To find / draw: its graph on this interval.
Method: find the amplitude and the period, take x-values a quarter period apart (and halfway between), make a table of values, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve, repeating the pattern over the whole interval.

Amplitude and period
\[\text{Amplitude} = 1\]
\[\text{Period} = 2\pi \div \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 4\]
Why: the interval \([-\pi, \pi]\) has length \(2\pi \approx 6.28\), about one and a half periods.

Table for \(x \ge 0\)
\[x = 1:\ \cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} = 0\]
\[x = 2:\ \cos\pi = -1\]
\[x = \pi:\ \cos\dfrac{\pi^2}{2} \approx \cos 4.93\]
\[\approx 0.22\]
Why: \(4.93\) rad is a little more than \(3\pi/2 \approx 4.71\), in Quadrant IV, where cosine is positive (calculator in radian mode).

Values for \(x < 0\)
\[\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}x\right) = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}x\]
Why: cosine is even, so \(y\) at \(-x\) equals \(y\) at \(x\); the left half is the mirror image of the right half.

Plot and join
Mark \(x\) as ordinary numbers \(-3\) to \(3\) (and \(\pm\pi\)), \(y\) from \(-1\) to \(1\). Join with a smooth wave.
Maximum \(1\) at \(x = 0\); minima \(-1\) at \(x = \pm2\); zeros at \(x = \pm1, \pm3\); the ends are \((\pm\pi, 0.22)\).
Why: the cosine wave has its peak at 0 and falls on both sides.

Check
\[x = 3:\ \cos\dfrac{3\pi}{2} = 0\]
Why: zeros of a cosine wave are a quarter period (1) on each side of a minimum: \(2 \pm 1 = 1, 3\).
blocks.final_answer: A cosine wave of amplitude 1 and period 4, symmetric about the y-axis: maximum \(1\) at \(x = 0\), minima \(-1\) at \(x = \pm2\), zeros at \(x = \pm1, \pm3\), ends at \((\pm\pi, 0.22)\).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = cos(pi x / 2) from -pi to pi: a cosine wave of height 1 and period 4, symmetric about the y-axis, maximum 1 at x = 0, minima -1 at x = -2 and 2, zeros at -3, -1, 1, 3, ending at (-pi, 0.22) and (pi, 0.22).
answer_figure.caption: Question 1 (vi): y = cos(πx/2) on [−π, π]; x marked in ordinary numbers (original drawing)
